barriers.description: Resource constraints and a small sample size prevented completion of later UCD stages and limited the study's ability to move beyond medium-fidelity testing.
barriers.justification: The lack of budget and human resources halted the Implementation Phase and restricted further iterations and higher-fidelity evaluation, directly hindering evaluation of designs and integration of feedback/iteration workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Due to resource constraints, the study's sample size is small and insufficient to illustrate the presence or absence of causal relationships on explored variables. The Implementation Phase of the UCD methodology was not done.

barriers.description: Participant attrition (three health workers resigned) reduced continuity of user involvement and altered the respondent pool during the two-month UCD process.
barriers.justification: Loss of participants during the study constrained the team's ability to maintain ongoing user involvement and manage evolving user understanding across iterative design activities.
barriers.reference_excerpt: (Three of these 30 health workers dropped out of the two-month long UCD process when they resigned from the RHU within the duration of this study. Hence, the change of 'respondents' data reported for subsequent questions.)

barriers.description: On-site or regional training events were costly and staff turnover meant that training benefits left with departing HCWs, limiting sustainable user competence.
barriers.justification: High cost of in-person training and turnover prevented reliable cascading of knowledge, constraining the designers' ability to facilitate user involvement, sustain training, and ensure long-term usability in the field.
barriers.reference_excerpt: On-site or regional training events are costly and require the HCW to leave the RHU for a certain period, which in turn slows down health care services. Moreover, when HCWs trained on the technology leave the RHU, the knowledge leaves with them.

barriers.description: A requested search function in the medium-fidelity prototype existed only as a non-functional placeholder, preventing full user testing of that feature.
barriers.justification: Because the search button was not implemented, designers could not fully evaluate or iterate that functionality with users, limiting the evaluate designs and integrate feedback workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: The users greatly appreciated the search button. They specifically requested this function when the Low Fidelity Prototype was being discussed. In the medium fidelity prototype design phase, the search buttons were just placeholders and not yet functional.

barriers.description: Many RHU staff were described as not open to learning complicated things and were often afraid to handle a device, reflecting resistance and low confidence among users.
barriers.justification: These attitudes and fears reduced designers' ability to engage users comfortably, complicating management of user understanding and facilitation of involvement required for iterative testing and requirement elicitation.
barriers.reference_excerpt: It was also observed that RHU staff are no longer open to learning complicated things or are often afraid to handle a device.
